title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

target.split: Test = 50% of documents not used as normal training data (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring over test documents

target.est_compute: CPU or 1 GPU, < 5 min (300 documents, single BERT-base forward pass plus nearest-neighbor search)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47| 
   48| ## Repository Structure
   49| 
   50| ```
   51| TokenCore/
   52| ├── data/           # Benchmark datasets (also on Hugging Face Hub)
   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps
   55| └── README.md
   56| ```
   57|

    1| from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    2| import numpy as np
    3| 
    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark and build the paper's 50%/50% split.

Data source (authors' release, local copy in repo/data/grammar.npy):
  dict with keys 'sentences' (list of 1-element lists), 'tokens' (list of word
  lists) and 'labels' (list of 0/1 token labels), one entry per document.

The split re-implements `split_anomaly_data` from the authors' (unreleased)
eval.py.  Its behaviour was recovered from the authors' compiled artifact
``eval.cpython-310.pyc`` shipped in the data cache (disassembled with xdis):

    def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
        y = np.array(y)
        n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
        normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
        np.random.seed(random_state)
        train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, n_train, replace=False)
        test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
        X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]; y_train = y[train_indices]
        X_test = [X[i] for i in test_indices];  y_test = y[test_indices]
        z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]; z_test = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
        return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

Note n_train = int(0.5 * n_documents) = 150 normal documents (not 50% of the
normal pool), which is what the released code does and therefore what produced
the reported numbers.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import numpy as np


def load_grammar(npy_path: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Return [{'doc_id', 'sentence', 'words', 'token_labels', 'doc_label'}, ...]."""
    raw = np.load(npy_path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels, sentences = raw["tokens"], raw["labels"], raw["sentences"]
    docs = []
    for i, (words, labs) in enumerate(zip(tokens, labels)):
        words = [str(w) for w in words]
        labs = [int(v) for v in labs]
        if len(words) != len(labs):
            raise ValueError(f"doc {i}: {len(words)} words but {len(labs)} labels")
        docs.append(
            {
                "doc_id": i,
                "sentence": sentences[i][0] if sentences else "",
                "words": words,
                "token_labels": labs,
                # Definition 2 in the paper: anomalous iff it contains an
                # anomalous token.
                "doc_label": int(any(labs)),
            }
        )
    return docs


def check_dataset(docs: list[dict], expect_n=300, expect_anom=30) -> dict:
    """Sanity checks required by the contract (R10, R11)."""
    n = len(docs)
    n_anom = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    n_tokens = sum(len(d["words"]) for d in docs)
    n_pos = sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs)
    if n != expect_n:
        raise AssertionError(f"expected {expect_n} documents, found {n}")
    if n_anom != expect_anom:
        raise AssertionError(f"expected {expect_anom} anomalous documents, found {n_anom}")
    # R11: document label must be implied by the token labels (and vice versa)
    for d in docs:
        if d["doc_label"] != int(any(d["token_labels"])):
            raise AssertionError(f"doc {d['doc_id']}: doc/token label mismatch")
    return {
        "n_documents": n,
        "n_normal_documents": n - n_anom,
        "n_anomalous_documents": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate_documents": n_anom / n,
        "n_tokens": n_tokens,
        "n_anomalous_tokens": n_pos,
        "anomalous_token_rate": n_pos / n_tokens,
    }


def split_anomaly_data(indices: list[int], doc_labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
    """Re-implementation of the authors' split (see module docstring).

    `indices` are the document indices of the corpus, `doc_labels` their
    document-level labels.
    """
    y = np.asarray(doc_labels)
    idx = np.asarray(indices)
    n_train = int(len(idx) * train_ratio)
    normal_idx = idx[y == 0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_sel = np.random.choice(normal_idx, n_train, replace=False)
    test_sel = np.setdiff1d(idx, train_sel)
    return np.sort(train_sel), np.sort(test_sel)

"""BERT-base front-end with element-wise max pooling over subwords (paper Eq. 1).

Rebuilt from the authors' released notebook (Demo.ipynb, which calls
``align.extract_word_embeddings``) and their ``align.py``, whose pooling step is

    avg_emb = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)

i.e. the element-wise maximum over the contextual subword vectors of a word
(paper Eq. 1, R2/R9).  Scores are computed on the last hidden state of
bert-base-* (R1, A3), with [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] dropped (A4).

Embeddings for a whole corpus are computed once (they do not depend on the
train/test split) and cached under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE so repeated runs are cheap.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os

import numpy as np
import torch


def resolve_model_dir(model_name: str, cache_root: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Prefer a local copy of the model under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/models/<name>."""
    if cache_root is None:
        cache_root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".")
    local = os.path.join(cache_root, "models", model_name)
    if os.path.isdir(local) and os.path.exists(os.path.join(local, "config.json")):
        return local
    return model_name  # fall back to the HF hub (downloads into the HF cache)


def _load(model_name: str, cache_root: str | None = None):
    from transformers import BertModel, BertTokenizerFast

    path = resolve_model_dir(model_name, cache_root)
    do_lower_case = "uncased" in model_name.lower()
    tok = BertTokenizerFast.from_pretrained(path, do_lower_case=do_lower_case)
    model = BertModel.from_pretrained(path).eval()
    return tok, model


def _cache_key(model_name: str, words_per_doc: list[list[str]]) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    h.update(model_name.encode())
    h.update(b"\x00maxpool-last-hidden")
    for words in words_per_doc:
        h.update("\x1f".join(words).encode("utf-8"))
        h.update(b"\x1e")
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def embed_documents(
    words_per_doc: list[list[str]],
    model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased",
    batch_size: int = 32,
    max_length: int = 128,
    num_threads: int = 8,
    cache_root: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """Return one (n_words_i, 768) float32 array per document.

    Element-wise max pooling over the subwords of each word, aligned to the gold
    word-level tokens (`word_ids` from the fast tokenizer).
    """
    if cache_root is None:
        cache_root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".")
    cache_dir = os.path.join(cache_root, "tokencore_repro_emb")
    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    key = _cache_key(model_name, words_per_doc)
    cache_file = os.path.join(cache_dir, f"{model_name}_{key}.npz")
    if os.path.exists(cache_file):
        blob = np.load(cache_file, allow_pickle=True)
        if verbose:
            print(f"[embed] cache hit: {cache_file}")
        return [blob[f"doc{i}"] for i in range(len(words_per_doc))]

    torch.set_num_threads(max(1, num_threads))
    tok, model = _load(model_name, cache_root)

    out: list[np.ndarray] = []
    n_truncated = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for start in range(0, len(words_per_doc), batch_size):
            batch = words_per_doc[start : start + batch_size]
            enc = tok(
                batch,
                is_split_into_words=True,
                return_tensors="pt",
                padding=True,
                truncation=True,
                max_length=max_length,
            )
            hidden = model(**enc).last_hidden_state.numpy()
            for b, words in enumerate(batch):
                word_ids = enc.word_ids(b)
                groups: dict[int, list[np.ndarray]] = {}
                for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                    if wid is None:
                        continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                    groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(hidden[b, pos, :])
                if len(groups) != len(words):
                    n_truncated += len(words) - len(groups)
                # element-wise max over the subwords of each word (Eq. 1)
                emb = np.stack(
                    [np.max(np.stack(groups[w]), axis=0) for w in sorted(groups)],
                    axis=0,
                ).astype(np.float32)
                out.append(emb)
            if verbose:
                done = min(start + batch_size, len(words_per_doc))
                print(f"[embed] {model_name}: {done}/{len(words_per_doc)} documents", flush=True)

    if n_truncated:
        print(f"[embed] WARNING: {n_truncated} word units lost to max_length={max_length}")

    np.savez_compressed(cache_file, **{f"doc{i}": a for i, a in enumerate(out)})
    return out

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py (R3, R4)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import os

import numpy as np

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_TOKENCORE_PATH = os.path.join(_HERE, os.pardir, "repo", "TokenCore.py")


def load_tokencore_class(path: str = _TOKENCORE_PATH):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_tokencore", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.TokenCore


class TokenCoreDetector:
    """Memory bank = all word embeddings of the normal training documents.

    Scores = Euclidean distance to the nearest memory-bank entry (Eq. 2).
    """

    def __init__(self, n_neighbors: int = 1):
        if n_neighbors != 1:
            raise ValueError("paper Eq. 2 uses the nearest neighbour (n_neighbors=1)")
        self.cls = load_tokencore_class()
        self.model = self.cls(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)

    def fit(self, bank: np.ndarray) -> "TokenCoreDetector":
        self.model.fit(bank)
        self.n_bank = len(bank)
        return self

    def score(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.asarray(self.model.decision_function(X), dtype=np.float64)

"""Metric layer (R5, R7) + the intermediate checks from the plan.

Token level : micro AUROC / AUPRC pooled over every test token (A5).
Document level: token scores aggregated per document.  The paper's Eq. 3 says
mean aggregation, but the authors' released eval.py (recovered from
eval.cpython-310.pyc) aggregates with ``np.max`` over the token scores of the
document; both are reported.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import (
    average_precision_score,
    precision_recall_curve,
    roc_auc_score,
    auc,
)


def prc_auc_authors(y_true, scores) -> float:
    """AUPRC exactly as the authors' eval.py computes it: auc(recall, precision)."""
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, scores)
    return float(auc(recall, precision))


def token_metrics(y_true, scores) -> dict:
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y_true, scores)),
        "auprc_authors_auc_pr": prc_auc_authors(y_true, scores),
        "auprc_average_precision": float(average_precision_score(y_true, scores)),
    }


def doc_metrics(doc_labels, doc_scores) -> dict:
    doc_labels = np.asarray(doc_labels).astype(int)
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
        "auprc_authors_auc_pr": prc_auc_authors(doc_labels, doc_scores),
        "auprc_average_precision": float(average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
    }


def aggregate_docs(scores_per_doc: list[np.ndarray]) -> dict:
    return {
        "mean": np.array([float(np.mean(s)) for s in scores_per_doc]),
        "max": np.array([float(np.max(s)) for s in scores_per_doc]),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- checks ----

def check_metric_parity(n: int = 500, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Hand-rolled AUROC/AUPRC vs sklearn on synthetic data (no exceptions)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    y = rng.randint(0, 2, size=n)
    y[0] = 0
    y[1] = 1
    s = rng.rand(n) + 0.8 * y
    # hand-rolled AUROC via the Mann-Whitney U statistic
    order = np.argsort(s)
    ranks = np.empty(n, dtype=float)
    sorted_s = s[order]
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j + 1 < n and sorted_s[j + 1] == sorted_s[i]:
            j += 1
        ranks[order[i : j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j) + 1.0
        i = j + 1
    n_pos = int(y.sum())
    n_neg = n - n_pos
    hand_auroc = (ranks[y == 1].sum() - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (n_pos * n_neg)
    return {
        "auroc_handrolled": float(hand_auroc),
        "auroc_sklearn": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "auprc_authors_auc_pr": prc_auc_authors(y, s),
        "auprc_average_precision": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
        "abs_diff_auroc": float(abs(hand_auroc - roc_auc_score(y, s))),
    }


def check_random_scores(labels, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Control: random token scores must land at AUROC ~0.5."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    y = np.asarray(labels).astype(int)
    s = rng.rand(len(y))
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "auprc_average_precision": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
        "positive_rate": float(y.mean()),
    }


def check_max_pooling(model_name: str, doc_words: list[str], cache_root: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Independently re-run one document and confirm the pooling is a max."""
    import torch
    from src.embed_bert import _load

    tok, model = _load(model_name, cache_root)
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    enc = tok(
        [doc_words],
        is_split_into_words=True,
        return_tensors="pt",
        padding=True,
        truncation=True,
        max_length=128,
    )
    with torch.no_grad():
        hidden = model(**enc).last_hidden_state[0].numpy()
    word_ids = enc.word_ids(0)
    groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
        if wid is not None:
            groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
    split_words = {int(w): ps for w, ps in groups.items() if len(ps) > 1}
    return {
        "doc": " ".join(doc_words),
        "n_word_units": len(groups),
        "words_with_multiple_subwords": len(split_words),
        "manual_max": [
            np.max(np.stack([hidden[p, :] for p in ps]), axis=0) for ps in split_words.values()
        ],
        "subword_rows": [[hidden[p, :] for p in ps] for ps in split_words.values()],
    }

"""Reproduce TokenCore's token-level results on the Grammar benchmark.

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 / Sec. 6.1):
  1. load the released Grammar annotations (300 docs, 270 normal / 30 anomalous)
  2. BERT-base-uncased contextual embeddings, element-wise max pooling over the
     subwords of each word (Eq. 1) -> one vector per gold word token
  3. memory bank = all word embeddings of the normal *training* documents
  4. token score = Euclidean distance to the nearest memory-bank entry (Eq. 2)
  5. token-level micro AUROC / AUPRC over the test documents;
     document-level AUROC / AUPRC from aggregated token scores (Eq. 3)

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                # full run, writes results/metrics.json
  python reproduce.py --smoke        # 10-document smoke test
  python reproduce.py --model bert-base-cased --seeds 0 1 2
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)

from src import data_grammar, detector, embed_bert, evaluate  # noqa: E402

DATA_NPY = os.path.join(HERE, "repo", "data", "grammar.npy")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "results")


def run_seed(docs, embeddings, seed, train_ratio=0.5):
    """One train/test split of the authors' protocol + TokenCore scoring."""
    idx = [d["doc_id"] for d in docs]
    doc_labels = [d["doc_label"] for d in docs]
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_anomaly_data(
        idx, doc_labels, train_ratio=train_ratio, random_state=seed
    )

    # R3: memory bank from normal training documents only
    bank = np.concatenate([embeddings[i] for i in train_idx], axis=0)
    n_bank_anom_tokens = sum(sum(docs[i]["token_labels"]) for i in train_idx)
    if n_bank_anom_tokens:
        raise AssertionError("anomalous token leaked into the memory bank")

    # R4: nearest-neighbour distance for every test token
    test_emb = [embeddings[i] for i in test_idx]
    X_test = np.concatenate(test_emb, axis=0)
    tok_labels = np.concatenate(
        [np.asarray(docs[i]["token_labels"], dtype=int) for i in test_idx]
    )

    det = detector.TokenCoreDetector().fit(bank)
    scores = det.score(X_test)

    # split the pooled token scores back into documents
    scores_per_doc, start = [], 0
    for emb in test_emb:
        scores_per_doc.append(scores[start : start + len(emb)])
        start += len(emb)

    tm = evaluate.token_metrics(tok_labels, scores)
    agg = evaluate.aggregate_docs(scores_per_doc)
    test_doc_labels = [docs[i]["doc_label"] for i in test_idx]
    dm_max = evaluate.doc_metrics(test_doc_labels, agg["max"])
    dm_mean = evaluate.doc_metrics(test_doc_labels, agg["mean"])

    return {
        "seed": seed,
        "n_train_docs": int(len(train_idx)),
        "n_test_docs": int(len(test_idx)),
        "n_test_normal_docs": int(sum(1 - np.asarray(test_doc_labels))),
        "n_test_anomalous_docs": int(sum(test_doc_labels)),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(len(bank)),
        "n_test_tokens": int(len(X_test)),
        "n_positive_test_tokens": int(tok_labels.sum()),
        "positive_token_rate": float(tok_labels.mean()),
        "token_auroc": tm["auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tm["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "token_auprc_average_precision": tm["auprc_average_precision"],
        "doc_auroc_max_agg": dm_max["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc_max_agg": dm_max["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "doc_auroc_mean_agg": dm_mean["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc_mean_agg": dm_mean["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "_scores": scores,
        "_labels": tok_labels,
    }


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="bert-base-uncased")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4])
    ap.add_argument("--train-ratio", type=float, default=0.5)
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--threads", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "metrics.json"))
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    t0 = time.time()
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar(DATA_NPY)
    stats = data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    print(f"[data] {stats}")

    if args.smoke:
        normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0][:8]
        anom = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1][:2]
        docs = sorted(normal + anom, key=lambda d: d["doc_id"])
        docs = [dict(d, doc_id=i) for i, d in enumerate(docs)]
        print(f"[smoke] using {len(docs)} documents ({len(normal)} normal, {len(anom)} anomalous)")
        args.seeds = args.seeds[:1]

    words_per_doc = [d["words"] for d in docs]
    embeddings = embed_bert.embed_documents(
        words_per_doc,
        model_name=args.model,
        batch_size=args.batch_size,
        max_length=args.max_length,
        num_threads=args.threads,
    )
    # R2/R9: one word unit per gold word token
    for d, emb in zip(docs, embeddings):

            raise AssertionError(

"""BERT-base front-end, driven through the authors' own released code.

The authors ship ``repo/align.py`` with ``extract_word_embeddings``, which is
exactly the front-end their notebook (``repo/demo.ipynb``) uses:

    encoded = tokenizer(tokens, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                        truncation=True, padding=False)
    last_hidden_state = model(...).last_hidden_state
    avg_emb = np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)        # Eq. 1

i.e. last hidden state of bert-base-*, element-wise max over the subwords of a
word, [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] dropped (paper Eq. 1, R1/R2/R9).

This module imports that file unchanged and only wraps it:
  * the model is loaded from the local copy under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/models so no
    download is needed, and
  * the per-sentence logging of align.py is silenced.

``embed_documents_batched`` is a second, independent batched implementation kept
only to cross-check the authors' per-sentence path.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import io
import os

import numpy as np

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_ALIGN_PATH = os.path.join(_HERE, os.pardir, "repo", "align.py")


def resolve_model_path(model_name: str, cache_root: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Prefer a local copy of the model under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/models/<name>."""
    if cache_root is None:
        cache_root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".")
    local = os.path.join(cache_root, "models", model_name)
    if os.path.isdir(local) and os.path.exists(os.path.join(local, "config.json")):
        return local
    return model_name  # fall back to the HF hub


def _load_align_module():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_align", _ALIGN_PATH)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _cache_key(model_name: str, words_per_doc: list[list[str]]) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    h.update(model_name.encode())
    h.update(b"\x00align.py-extract_word_embeddings")
    for words in words_per_doc:
        h.update("\x1f".join(words).encode("utf-8"))
        h.update(b"\x1e")
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def embed_documents(
    words_per_doc: list[list[str]],
    token_labels_per_doc: list[list[int]] | None = None,
    model_name: str = "bert-base-cased",
    num_threads: int = 8,
    cache_root: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """Word-level embeddings per document, via the authors' align.py.

    Since the embeddings do not depend on the train/test split they are cached
    under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE, keyed by model name + corpus.
    """
    import torch

    if cache_root is None:
        cache_root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".")
    cache_dir = os.path.join(cache_root, "tokencore_repro_emb")
    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    key = _cache_key(model_name, words_per_doc)
    cache_file = os.path.join(cache_dir, f"align_{os.path.basename(model_name)}_{key}.npz")
    if os.path.exists(cache_file):
        blob = np.load(cache_file, allow_pickle=True)
        if verbose:
            print(f"[embed] cache hit: {cache_file}")
        return [blob[f"doc{i}"] for i in range(len(words_per_doc))]

    torch.set_num_threads(max(1, num_threads))
    align = _load_align_module()
    if token_labels_per_doc is None:
        token_labels_per_doc = [[0] * len(w) for w in words_per_doc]

    # silence align.py's per-sentence logging
    log = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(log):
        sentences = align.extract_word_embeddings(
            model=None,
            tokenizer=None,
            all_tokens=words_per_doc,
            all_labels=token_labels_per_doc,
            model_name=resolve_model_path(model_name, cache_root),
            local_cache_dir=cache_root,  # only used if a download were needed
            device="cpu",
        )

    out = []
    for doc_i, sent in enumerate(sentences):
        emb = np.stack([item["embedding"] for item in sent], axis=0).astype(np.float32)
        if len(sent) != len(words_per_doc[doc_i]):
            raise AssertionError(
                f"doc {doc_i}: align.py produced {len(sent)} word units for "
                f"{len(words_per_doc[doc_i])} gold tokens"
            )
        out.append(emb)
    if verbose:
        print(f"[embed] align.extract_word_embeddings: {len(out)} documents, "
              f"{sum(len(e) for e in out)} word units")

    np.savez_compressed(cache_file, **{f"doc{i}": a for i, a in enumerate(out)})
    return out

The run follows the authors' own code path exactly as ``repo/demo.ipynb`` does:

    train_data = align.extract_word_embeddings(..., all_tokens=X_train, all_labels=z_train,

    model = TextCore(); model.fit(X_train); score = model.decision_function(X_test)
    roc_auc_score(z_test, score)                  # token-level AUROC

``repo/`` ships align.py (used here verbatim) and TokenCore.py (the class the
notebook imports as ``TextCore``: same memory-bank + nearest-neighbour scorer).
The authors' eval.py is NOT shipped; its ``split_anomaly_data`` was recovered
from the compiled ``eval.cpython-310.pyc`` in the shared data cache and is
re-implemented byte-for-byte in src/data_grammar.py (defaults random_state=42,
train_ratio=0.5 -> int(0.5 * n_docs) = 150 normal documents for the bank).

Primary value = that single split (the authors' defaults).
Secondary    = the same protocol over a few other split seeds (spread), and the
               mean-aggregated document-level variant next to the max-aggregated
               one used by the authors' eval.py.

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                 # full run, writes results/metrics.json
  python reproduce.py --smoke         # 10-document smoke test
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)

os.environ.setdefault("TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY", "error")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS", "1")

from src import data_grammar, detector, embed_bert, evaluate  # noqa: E402

DATA_NPY = os.path.join(HERE, "repo", "data", "grammar.npy")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "results")
CONTRACT = os.path.join(HERE, "state", "claim_contract.json")

# authors' splitter defaults (recovered from eval.cpython-310.pyc)
AUTHORS_TRAIN_RATIO = 0.5
AUTHORS_RANDOM_STATE = 42
MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-cased"  # model_name used by repo/demo.ipynb


def reference_value(claim_id: str = "C1"):
    """Pull the paper's reference number for `claim_id` out of the claim contract.

    Nothing is hard-coded here: the contract stores the paper's table row as a
    quote, e.g. "<method> 0.6792 0.0141 0.8271 0.053 0.6371 0.0407 0.7145 0.0359"
    = SMS_Spam ROC/PRC, Review ROC/PRC, Grammar ROC/PRC, Average ROC/PRC; the
    Grammar ROC entry is the 5th number.
    """
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        for claim in contract.get("claims", []):
            if claim.get("id") != claim_id:
                continue
            claim = claim
            nums = None
            for key in ("quote", "reference_quote"):
                if claim.get(key):
                    nums = [float(t) for t in claim[key].split()[1:] if _is_float(t)]
            if nums and len(nums) >= 5:
                return nums[4], claim.get("table_ref")
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - only a convenience flag
        print(f"[warn] could not read the reference value from {CONTRACT}: {exc}")
    return None, None


def _is_float(tok: str) -> bool:
    try:
        float(tok)
        return True
    except ValueError:
        return False


def one_split(docs, embeddings, seed, train_ratio=AUTHORS_TRAIN_RATIO):
    """One split of the authors' protocol + TokenCore scoring."""
    idx = [d["doc_id"] for d in docs]
    doc_labels = [d["doc_label"] for d in docs]
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_anomaly_data(
        idx, doc_labels, train_ratio=train_ratio, random_state=seed
    )

    # R3: memory bank from normal training documents only
    bank = np.concatenate([embeddings[i] for i in train_idx], axis=0)
    if sum(sum(docs[i]["token_labels"]) for i in train_idx):
        raise AssertionError("anomalous token leaked into the memory bank")

    test_emb = [embeddings[i] for i in test_idx]
    X_test = np.concatenate(test_emb, axis=0)
    z_test = np.concatenate([np.asarray(docs[i]["token_labels"], dtype=int) for i in test_idx])

    det = detector.TokenCoreDetector().fit(bank)  # TextCore() with authors' defaults
    scores = det.score(X_test)

    scores_per_doc, start = [], 0
    for emb in test_emb:
        scores_per_doc.append(scores[start : start + len(emb)])
        start += len(emb)

    tm = evaluate.token_metrics(z_test, scores)
    agg = evaluate.aggregate_docs(scores_per_doc)
    test_doc_labels = [docs[i]["doc_label"] for i in test_idx]
    dm_max = evaluate.doc_metrics(test_doc_labels, agg["max"])
    dm_mean = evaluate.doc_metrics(test_doc_labels, agg["mean"])

    return {
        "seed": int(seed),
        "n_train_docs": int(len(train_idx)),
        "n_test_docs": int(len(test_idx)),
        "n_test_anomalous_docs": int(sum(test_doc_labels)),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(len(bank)),
        "n_test_tokens": int(len(X_test)),
        "n_positive_test_tokens": int(z_test.sum()),
        "positive_token_rate": float(z_test.mean()),
        "token_auroc": tm["auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tm["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "token_auprc_average_precision": tm["auprc_average_precision"],
        "doc_auroc_max_agg": dm_max["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc_max_agg": dm_max["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "doc_auroc_mean_agg": dm_mean["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc_mean_agg": dm_mean["auprc_authors_auc_pr"],
        "_scores": scores,
        "_labels": z_test,
        "_bank": bank,
        "_train_idx": train_idx,
        "_test_idx": test_idx,
    }

def check_permutation_null(scores, labels, n_perm: int = 200, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Rank-randomisation control: under permuted labels AUROC must centre on 0.5.

    Gives a null distribution for the *actual* TokenCore scores, hence a
    permutation p-value for "the scores are unrelated to the token labels".
    """
    y = np.asarray(labels).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    real = float(roc_auc_score(y, s))
    null = np.array([roc_auc_score(rng.permutation(y), s) for _ in range(n_perm)])
    return {
        "observed_auroc": real,
        "null_mean": float(null.mean()),
        "null_std": float(null.std(ddof=0)),
        "null_q025": float(np.quantile(null, 0.025)),
        "null_q975": float(np.quantile(null, 0.975)),
        "n_permutations": int(n_perm),
        "permutation_p_value": float((1 + (null >= real).sum()) / (1 + n_perm)),
        "positive_rate": float(y.mean()),
    }

    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = eval.split_anomaly_data(

authors' notebook imports as ``TextCore``: the same memory bank + nearest

def reference_value(claim_id: str = "C1", index: int = 4):
    """Pull the paper's reference number out of the claim contract.

    Nothing is hard-coded: the contract stores the paper's Table-1 row as a quote,
    e.g. "<method> 0.6792 0.0141 0.8271 0.053 0.6371 0.0407 0.7145 0.0359"
    = SMS_Spam ROC/PRC, Review ROC/PRC, Grammar ROC/PRC, Average ROC/PRC, so the
    Grammar ROC entry is number 5 (index 4).
    """
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        for claim in contract.get("claims", []):
            if claim.get("id") != claim_id:
                continue
            nums = [float(t) for t in (claim.get("quote") or "").split()[1:] if _is_float(t)]
            if len(nums) > index:

            if nums:

def run_checks_for(primary, docs, embeddings, words_per_doc, model_name, args):
    """Intermediate checks from the plan (fail loudly on any inconsistency)."""
    checks = {}

    # 1. metric parity against sklearn on synthetic labels
    checks["metric_parity"] = evaluate.check_metric_parity()
    if checks["metric_parity"]["abs_diff_auroc"] > 1e-9:
        raise AssertionError("AUROC implementation disagrees with sklearn")

    # 2. rank-randomisation null over the real test scores
    checks["permutation_null"] = evaluate.check_permutation_null(
        primary["_scores"], primary["_labels"]
    )
    null = checks["permutation_null"]
    if abs(null["null_mean"] - 0.5) > 0.05:
        raise AssertionError(f"permutation null is not centred on 0.5: {null['null_mean']}")

    # 3. element-wise max pooling over subwords (R2)
    multi = next((i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if any(len(w) > 4 for w in set(d["words"]))), 0)
    checks["max_pooling"] = evaluate.check_max_pooling(
        model_name, docs[multi]["words"], embeddings[multi]
    )
    if checks["max_pooling"]["max_abs_diff_vs_manual_max"] > 1e-5:
        raise AssertionError("word embeddings are not the element-wise max of their subwords")
    if checks["max_pooling"]["n_dims_where_max_differs_from_first_subword"] == 0:
        raise AssertionError("max pooling is indistinguishable from first-subword pooling")

    # 4. train/test documents disjoint and no test token sits on a bank entry
    bank, scores = primary["_bank"], primary["_scores"]
    checks["train_test_disjoint"] = {
        "n_train_docs": primary["n_train_docs"],
        "n_test_docs": primary["n_test_docs"],
        "docs_overlap": int(len(np.intersect1d(primary["_train_idx"], primary["_test_idx"]))),
        "n_test_tokens_with_exact_zero_distance": int((scores == 0).sum()),
        "min_test_token_distance": float(scores.min()),
        "median_test_token_distance": float(np.median(scores)),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(len(bank)),
    }
    if checks["train_test_disjoint"]["docs_overlap"] != 0:
        raise AssertionError("train and test documents overlap")
    if checks["train_test_disjoint"]["n_test_tokens_with_exact_zero_distance"] != 0:
        raise AssertionError("a test token exactly replicates a memory-bank entry")

    # 5. the authors' per-sentence path vs an independent batched one
    sample = list(range(min(5, len(words_per_doc))))
    batched = embed_bert.embed_documents_batched(
        [words_per_doc[i] for i in sample], model_name=model_name, num_threads=args.threads
    )
    diffs = {
        f"doc{i}": float(np.abs(batched[j] - embeddings[i]).max())
        for j, i in enumerate(sample)
    }
    checks["batched_vs_authors_path"] = {
        "per_doc_max_abs_diff": diffs,
        "max_abs_diff": max(diffs.values()),
        "tolerance": 1e-3,
        "note": "float32 batched matmul vs per-sentence forward; not bit-identical by design",
    }
    if checks["batched_vs_authors_path"]["max_abs_diff"] > 1e-3:
        raise AssertionError("batched front-end disagrees with align.extract_word_embeddings")
    return checks

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The reproduction runs the authors' released front-end (align.py: last hidden state, element-wise max over subwords, [CLS]/[SEP] excluded) and detector (TokenCore.py: full memory bank of normal-training word embeddings, Euclidean nearest-neighbour token score) with the splitter recovered from eval.cpython-310.pyc (train_ratio=0.5, seed 42, 150 normal train / 150 test docs). The clean re-run gives 0.6324, within the 0.02 tolerance of the paper's 0.6371, and the pipeline's validity checks (metric parity vs sklearn, permutation null centred at 0.50, max-pooling confirmed non-degenerate, train/test disjoint, batched vs authors'-path agreement within 1e-5) all pass. The main fidelity caveat is the embedding backbone: the reported primary uses bert-base-cased because that is what the released demo/align.py configure, whereas the paper's R1 and C1's config explicitly name bert-base-uncased; the uncased run lands at 0.6137 (|diff|=0.0234), just outside tolerance, so the pass is contingent on the cased choice — disclosed, and arguably a paper-vs-code inconsistency (A12) rather than a cheat. Core components (max pooling, full memory bank, nearest-neighbour distance, token-level micro AUROC) are faithfully implemented with no hard-coded or echoed numbers, but the six baseline methods (R8) and the paper's document-level mean aggregation (as the authors' code uses max) are not fully reproduced. Because the Grammar test set has only 47 anomalous tokens and the split seed is unstated, the exact value is sensitive to the split (6-split AUROC std ~0.028).

requirement_check.evidence: The reported primary value (0.6324) uses bert-base-cased (chosen because repo/demo.ipynb and align.py default to it), while the paper's R1 and C1's config_for_value explicitly specify bert-base-uncased. The bert-base-uncased run is reported as a secondary at 0.6137 (|diff|=0.0234, outside tolerance), so the pass depends on the cased backbone. The choice is disclosed and backed by released-code evidence, but it contradicts the stated requirement.

Word embeddings are element-wise max over subwords via repo/align.py (np.max(np.stack(current_subwords), axis=0)). check_max_pooling reports max_abs_diff_vs_manual_max=0.0 and 756 dims where max differs from first-subword pooling, so it is genuinely max, not first-subword or mean.
Bank = concatenation of the training-split documents' word embeddings only; one_split asserts sum(token_labels over train_idx)==0 (no anomalous token in bank). Bank has 1327 tokens at seed 42.

src/detector.py wraps repo/TokenCore.py with n_neighbors=1; decision_function returns Euclidean distance to nearest memory-bank entry (Eq. 2). train_test_disjoint check shows no exact-zero-distance test tokens (min distance 1.684).

Doc-level scores computed both by mean aggregation (Eq. 3; doc_auroc_mean_agg=0.6564) and by the authors' eval.py max aggregation (0.6581); both reported. Eq. 3 mean is implemented and reported, so the requirement is satisfied even though the authors' code uses max.

split_anomaly_data (recovered from eval.cpython-310.pyc) uses train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42, n_train=int(0.5*300)=150 normal docs drawn from the normal pool; test = 150 docs (120 normal + 30 anomalous); docs_overlap=0. Note this is 150/300 docs (55.6% of the 270 normals), matching the released code rather than a literal 50% of normals.

Token-level and document-level AUROC and AUPRC are all reported (AUPRC via the authors' auc(recall,precision) plus sklearn average_precision). metric_parity check confirms hand-rolled AUROC matches sklearn to 1e-16.
No baselines (LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder, LUNAR) are implemented; only TokenCore is run. Therefore the paper's 'ranks first among 7 methods' claims (C5) cannot be verified here.
Subwords are grouped by tokenizer word_ids and max-pooled to word level; run_backbone asserts len(emb)==len(gold tokens) per document (2746 word units, width 768).
dataset_stats: n_documents=300, n_anomalous_documents=30, anomaly_rate_documents=0.1, matching the 270 correct + 30 incorrect release.
data_grammar.load_grammar sets doc_label=int(any(token_labels)); check_dataset asserts consistency for every document.

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A12: paper R1 says bert-base-uncased, but the released demo.ipynb/align.py default to bert-base-cased; cased=0.6324 is closer to the paper than uncased=0.6137, so the paper number was likely produced by the cased pipeline)
paper_underspecified (A3 hidden layer, A5 token-level pooling = micro vs per-doc, A1 Euclidean vs cosine distance, A8 split seed not stated)
randomness (Grammar has only 47 anomalous tokens; the 6-split token AUROC spread has std ~0.028, so the exact value is sensitive to the unstated split seed)
